triggers.name: api
triggers.note: An HTTPS request — REST at /v1, MCP at /mcp, OAuth at /oauth, inbound hooks at /hooks. All served by the same `api` function as the app, so they reach the same command handlers.

triggers.name: queue
triggers.note: A Cloud Tasks queue: retries with exponential backoff, a max dispatch rate, and deduplication by Cloud Tasks task name.

triggers.name: hosting
triggers.note: A static file on Firebase Hosting, in front of the CDN — no function runs. The SDK lives here so an orchestrator can import it by URL from any runtime.

proxyFunctions.name: commands
proxyFunctions.location: the one module every door calls
ioSchema: // app/services/* ARE these functions. The HTTP layer is a thin
// ctx.actor is a principal: the person, or the agent a token acts as
implementation: ONE IMPLEMENTATION, THREE FRONT DOORS. The permission check, the
validation, the transaction, the activity row, the notification and
the webhook are written once. A door only translates: REST maps
resource-shaped JSON and Markdown; MCP maps tool arguments; the app
sends the command shape directly.
The alternative — clients writing Firestore directly, with triggers
for side effects — would give the app a write path the API does
not have, and every rule twice: once in firestore.rules, once in
the API. See the architecture page.

proxyFunctions.name: toPublic
proxyFunctions.location: the shape the outside world sees
ioSchema: interface PublicPrincipal {         // people AND agents, one shape
email: string /* '' for agents */, avatar_url: string | null,
icon: string | null              // agents: a prebuilt icon id ('claude', 'bot', …); null for people
id: string, key: string, url: string
stage: { id, name, category }, priority: { id, name } | null
start_at: string | null, due_at: string | null   // ISO
links: { type, key }[], referenced_by: string[]   // keys
id, ticket_key, kind, body_md,     // Message.markdown when posted as Markdown
author: { id, kind, name }, via, via_token: string | null,
reply_to, attachments: PublicAttachment[], reactions, pinned, created_at, edited_at, deleted
id, name, mime, size, kind: FileKind, language, textual,
interface PublicEvent { id /* = cursor */, type, board, ticket_key, message_id, actor, summary, created_at, acked_at }
implementation: ids are resolved to names so a script or a model can read it
without a second call; fields are keyed by NAME outside, by id
inside (a rename breaks a script, but it cannot corrupt data).
RichText → Markdown; mentions as [@Name](mailto:email) for people and
[@Name](agent:ag_…) for agents, refs as #KEY.
Accepted back the same way, or as a bare '@email' / '@ag_…', and
assignees by id, email or agent name.

services.name: rest
ioSchema: GET    /v1/me                             principal, board, scopes; for an agent:
title, description_md, fields by NAME, dates, tags,
assignees by id | email | agent name
POST   /v1/tickets/{KEY}/files     multipart, or JSON { name, mime?, text | content_base64 }
?content=1 → text for md / html / text / csv / json / code
GET    /v1/events?cursor=&limit=&unacked=                events:read — the inbox, oldest first
GET    /v1/events/stream?cursor=   Server-Sent Events of the same; Last-Event-ID resumes
GET    /v1/live                    a short-lived RTDB credential   events:read
stream rev/{board} and agents/{id}/wake instead of polling
// PHASE 17 (§Y1) — the turn receipt an orchestrator posts when a run ends:
POST   /v1/tickets/{KEY}/messages  { …, run?: { n, outcome, cost_usd, session_usd,
// PHASE 17 (§Z2) — ACCOUNT tokens only (account scopes; a board token is 403):
POST   /v1/boards                  { name, key, template?, color?, icon? }  boards:create
POST   /v1/agents                  { name, description?, system_prompt?, id?, avatar? }
POST   /v1/boards/{KEY}/agents     { agent, role | null, stage_grant? }  agents:write | boards:admin
// PHASE 3 (§L4) — an agent that shows its work:
POST   /v1/heartbeat   { ticket?, state, message?, progress? }  status:write
// events gained question_answered / question_cancelled, carrying the
// answer values — an orchestrator acts on them without a second call.
// A token names ONE board, so /v1/board and /v1/tickets take no board
// …/attachments) still answer, marked deprecated in the OpenAPI.
// Also accepts oauth tokens. Idempotency-Key header on every POST.
// Errors: RFC 9457 problem+json. Pagination: opaque cursor.
// OpenAPI 3.1 generated from the zod schemas → /v1/openapi.json
implementation: route → scope gate (REST_ROUTES) → zod parse → commands.X(ctx, input) → toPublic(result)
EVERY WRITE HERE IS A COMMAND THE APP ALSO USES. There is no
API-only path to drift.
Files: the door writes the object under the ticket's Storage prefix
and a files/{fileId} row with source 'upload'; the message that names
it later attaches it (messagePost fileIds).
Events: an agent token reads agentInbox/{agentId}; a person's token
reads their own inbox, on its board. The event id IS the cursor.
The stream sends 'event' frames and a 'ping' every 25 s.
Every change is attributed '<principal> via token <name>' — the
thread shows 'Builder (agent) via token orch-eng-builder'.

services.name: mcp
ioSchema: auth: Bearer tm_live_… (a board token, the same as REST)
or OAuth 2.1 for interactive clients (Claude, Cursor)
tools (hidden from tools/list, and refused, without their scope):
whoami()                          → principal, board, scopes; for an agent its system prompt
list_boards()                     → boards this credential may act on
search_tickets({ query?, assignee?, stage?, state?, due_before?, limit? })
get_ticket({ key, messages?: N })  → ticket + pins + files + last N messages
create_ticket({ title, description?, assignees?, due?, priority?, fields? })
update_ticket({ key, title?, stage?, assignees?, due?, fields?, … })
assign_ticket({ key, add?, remove? })       // people or agents
post_message({ key, markdown, attachments?: fileId[], reply_to? })
upload_file({ key, name, mime?, text? | content_base64? })  → fileId
read_file({ fileId })             → text for md / html / text / csv / json, else a signed URL
get_events({ cursor?, limit? })   ack_events({ ids | upTo })
// PHASE 3 (§L4) — hidden without questions:write / tasklists:write / status:write:
ask_question({ key, title, body?, fields, allow_comment?, to?, blocking?, expires_at? })
get_question({ id })              → status and, once given, the answer values
set_tasklist({ key, title, items, list_id?, position?, closed? })
update_task_item({ key, list_id, item_id, status?, note? })
delete_tasklist({ key, list_id })   // the only 'delete' there is, and it removes a CHECKLIST
// THERE IS NO answer_question. An agent asks; a PERSON answers, in the app.
board://schema         (the token's board: stages, fields, members)
on none — there is deliberately no delete tool.
implementation: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk server, stateless (no session affinity
needed on Cloud Functions / Cloud Run)
each tool = zod input (McpToolSchemas) → commands.X(ctx{via:'mcp'}) → toPublic → text
EVERY CHANGE IS ATTRIBUTED. With an OAuth grant: 'Panth via Claude
(MCP)', the person as actor. With an agent token: the AGENT is the
actor — 'Builder (agent) via token orch-eng-builder' — and its owner
is answerable. An agent is never a ghost editor.
upload_file TAKES TEXT. An agent writing plan.md or report.html
passes the document as a string; no base64, no multipart.
BOARD NAMES AND FIELD NAMES, NOT IDS, in arguments. A model reads
'stage: Review'; the tool resolves it and says which names exist
when it cannot.

services.name: sdk
ioSchema: https://taskmanager-example.web.app/lib/       install lines per runtime, examples
/lib/v1/sdk.js          ESM bundle, no dependencies (browsers, Deno, Bun)
/lib/v1/sdk.d.ts        ONE flat declaration file — no zod, no @tm/shared left
/lib/v1/sdk.ts          the same SDK as a single TypeScript file (Deno, Bun)
/lib/v1/tm-sdk-<version>.tgz  and  tm-sdk.tgz    npm install, for Node
/lib/v1/openapi.json    a copy of /v1/openapi.json, from the same zod schemas
/lib/v1/sdk.json        what this build is: version, sizes, sha-256 per file
const tm = createClient({ token })      // one board, one identity: the token decides
tm.events.{list,ack,stream} (SSE, resumes from its cursor) · tm.webhooks.*
tm.work(handler, { concurrency, filter })   // the whole orchestrator loop
implementation: Built from sdk/ in this repo (@tm/sdk): zero runtime dependencies, one
injectable fetch, Node 20+, Deno, Bun and browsers.
THE TYPES ARE THE SERVER'S TYPES. Every shape is asserted structurally
identical, in BOTH directions, to the @tm/shared schema the routes parse
with, so a field that drifts on the server is a compile error in the SDK
build — and a wrong field in an orchestrator is a compile error there,
rather than a 400 an hour into a run.
TYPE HINTS ARRIVE BY EVERY ROUTE, because a URL import only carries types
if the server says where they are: the tarball's package.json (`types`, and
an `exports` map with the `types` condition first), `sdk.ts` being real
source, and `sdk.js` starting with /// <reference types="./sdk.d.ts" />
beside the X-TypeScript-Types header.
RETRIES ARE SAFE. 429, 5xx and network failures back off and honour
Retry-After; every write carries an Idempotency-Key generated once per
call and reused across its retries, so a retried create is still one
ticket.
STAGED BY THE DEPLOY, never by hand: scripts/deploy-lib.mjs copies sdk/dist
into the hosting build and refuses a missing, stale or unstamped one —
shipping yesterday's bundle next to today's API is the exact failure this
plumbing exists to prevent.
/lib/v1/* is what a consumer pins, so it is immutable for a year: a new
build gets a new tarball name, and a change to the wire format gets a new
prefix (/lib/v2/). /lib/latest/* is the moving target, and never cached.

services.name: mcpTools
services.location: mcpTools(tm, options) — in the orchestrator's own process
ioSchema: describe: { reply: 'Reply to the ticket you are working on. Markdown.' },
defaults: { ticket: 'ENG-42' },   // fixed arguments the model never passes
wrap:     { reply: (call) => (args) => call({ ...args, markdown: prefix + args.markdown }) },
scopes:   ['tickets:read', 'comments:write'],   // else read once from GET /v1/me
→ [{ name, description, inputSchema (JSON Schema), handler, scopes, readOnly, originalName }]
implementation: RATHER THAN HANDING AN AGENT THE WHOLE /mcp ENDPOINT, an orchestrator
builds the tool list it wants and serves it from its own MCP server.
THE NAMES AND SHAPES ARE THE ENDPOINT’S. They come from the same tool
catalogue in @tm/shared that platform/services/mcp serves, and a test
asserts the two lists stay identical — a model moved from the hosted
endpoint to a hand-built server meets the tools it already knows.
SCOPES FILTER THE LIST, not only the call: a tool the token may not use is
dropped, so a model is never offered something that must fail. The server
still checks, so this is a courtesy and not the security.
`defaults` are applied where the model cannot reach them and are removed
from the JSON Schema, so a fixed `ticket` cannot be argued with; `ticket`
also fills the `key` argument most tools use.
PLAIN DEFINITIONS, so they work with any MCP implementation.
registerTools() is the convenience for the official SDK — it wires the
server’s fallbackRequestHandler for tools/list and tools/call.

services.name: oauth
implementation: consent: see the client's name and the scopes, Approve
code (60s) → access (1h) + refresh (30d, rotated on use; reuse of
an old refresh token revokes the whole grant — theft detection)
Firebase Auth is the IDENTITY; this is only the DELEGATION layer.

services.name: grantRevoke
implementation: owner only; delete the grant and every oauthTokens row for it
the MCP client's next call gets 401 and must ask again

services.name: apiKeyCreate
ioSchema: actsAs?: { kind: 'user' } | { kind: 'agent', id: AgentId }   // default: me
expiresInDays?: number | null     // null = never; the form offers 30 / 90 / 365
interface Res { key: string, keyId, prefix, expiresAt }   // key: the ONLY time it is returned
implementation: any signed-in person, for themselves
boardId: a board they are on → 403 otherwise
actsAs agent: an agent THEY own, not archived, currently on that board
→ 404 / 403 otherwise; its token cannot carry board:admin or webhooks:manage
admin scopes on a person token: the owner must be admin there
store sha256 + prefix; return 'tm_live_' + base62(32)
The form shows the key once, with a ready-to-paste MCP config
(mcpClientConfig) and curl examples (curlExamples) — both built in
@tm/shared so the page and the docs say the same thing.
Changes made with it appear as 'Panth via token <name>', or for an
agent token 'Builder (agent) via token <name>'.

services.name: apiKeyRevoke
implementation: owner only; revokedAt = now, revokedReason 'owner' — the next call with it gets 401
revoking twice is ok
Tokens are also revoked FOR you: agentArchive ('agentArchived'),
boardAgentSet role:null ('agentRemoved'), leaving the board ('ownerLeft').

services.name: webhookUpsert
ioSchema: interface Req { boardId, webhookId?, url, events, active?, rotateSecret? }
implementation: can(admin) on the board
https only; resolve the host and refuse private / link-local ranges
send a 'ping' event; save even if it fails, but say so

services.name: webhookDispatch
ioSchema: // enqueued by every command after commit: { boardId, event, envelope }
implementation: fan out: every active webhook on that board whose events match
→ one Cloud Task per (webhook, envelope), named by both (dedupe)
POST with X-TM-Signature, 10s timeout
2xx → delivery 'ok', failures = 0
else → retry: 1m, 5m, 30m, 2h, 6h, 12h; then 'gave_up', failures++
failures ≥ 20 → active = false, owner emailed
Slack and GitHub installs consume the same events through here.
Envelope.actor carries kind ('user' | 'agent') and via_token, so a
receiver can ignore its own agent's changes without a lookup.

services.name: deliver
ioSchema: // enqueued by notify(): { uid, groupKey, inboxIds, channels }
// Cloud Tasks task name = `${uid}:${groupKey}:${minute}` — a burst of 5 comments
// in a minute becomes ONE push and ONE email
implementation: user = users/{uid}; skip everything already read in the app (inbox.readAt)
in quiet hours → reschedule to the end of them (except 'mentioned'
if the user allowed it)
push:     FCM sendEach to users/{uid}/devices; unregistered → delete token
payload: title 'ENG-42 · Priya', body, link, tag = ticketId
(a later push REPLACES the earlier one for the same ticket)
email:    Resend (or SES); HTML from a template like the reference's
kicker/accent per event; Reply-To = emailThreads token;
In-Reply-To/References = the ticket's phantom root id;
List-Unsubscribe → one-click to the settings page
only if the person ticked Email for this event
whatsapp: user.whatsapp.optIn required
inside 24h window → free-form text with the link
outside → approved template 'ticket_update' / 'ticket_due'
whatsappSessions.contextTicketId = ticketId (for a bare reply)
every attempt → deliveries/{id} with provider id and status

services.name: emailInbound
ioSchema: // provider inbound parse: to, from, subject, text, html, attachments[]
implementation: to = t.{token}@in…   → a reply:
thread = emailThreads/{token}; From must be that user's address
strip quoted history and signature (talon-style)
commands.messagePost(ctx{ actor: uid, via: 'email' }, markdown)
to = {intake}@in…    → a new ticket (email-to-board):
commands.ticketCreate on intake.boardId, reporter = From,
subject → title, body → description, attachments → Storage
anything else → dropped, logged

services.name: whatsappInbound
ioSchema: // Meta Cloud API webhook: messages[] and statuses[]
implementation: statuses → deliveries status (delivered / read / failed)
messages → session = whatsappSessions/{from}; lastInboundAt = now
button 'Mark done'  → commands.ticketUpdate(stage → first 'done')
button 'Snooze 1d'  → inbox snoozedUntil
text                → commands.messagePost on contextTicketId, via 'whatsapp'
no context          → reply with the last 3 notified tickets as a list
'STOP'              → optIn = false

services.name: intakeSubmit
ioSchema: meta?: Record<string, unknown>     // page URL, user agent, app version…
GET /v1/intake/schema → the board's public options (for the widget's selects)
implementation: commands.ticketCreate(ctx{ actor: 'intake-bot', via: 'intake' }, …defaults, fieldMap)
reporter gets an email with the key and can REPLY to add to the thread
the reference's tt.ts widget keeps working with a two-header change

services.name: githubHook
implementation: find keys in branch name, PR title and commit messages: /\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,5}-\d+\b/
for each key found, on a board that linked this repo:
system message 'PR #812 opened by …' with the link
merged && repo.moveOnMerge → commands.ticketUpdate(stage) via 'integration'

services.name: installConnect
ioSchema: // OAuth to the provider (GitHub App install, Slack OAuth v2, Google)
implementation: board admin only
state param = signed { uid, boardId, nonce }
tokens → Secret Manager; boards/{b}/integrations/{provider} written

services.name: icsFeed
ioSchema: // a calendar subscription URL — Google / Apple / Outlook poll it
implementation: every active ticket assigned to uid with a dueAt, as all-day or timed VEVENTs
token is per user, rotatable in Account › Connected apps
READ-ONLY AND POLLED, on purpose: two-way calendar sync is a phase-4
problem; seeing deadlines in your calendar is a phase-2 feature.
